observations.seen: The coast frame and the menu frame are lit by a flat, overcast-looking sky with no low sun direction, so the car has no rim light or warm key. The canyon frame has a warm sunset sky, but the car and road stay cool purple-grey. At night the streetlamps on the skyway cast no light pools onto the road.

The car's contact shadow is a faint, soft smudge that barely grounds it. Trees on the coastal hill cast visible shadows. The canyon walls and the rocks on the ridge cast no readable shadows, and nothing at night casts a shadow.
The teal paint shows broad soft highlights but does not reflect the sky, sea or canyon walls. The night road has a faint sheen under the car and no reflections of the city or lamps.

The three biomes add variety: a coast with sea, turbines and red-roof houses, a canyon, and a night city. Each is sparse, though. The canyon walls are huge flat planes, the city towers are plain boxes with stripe windows, and the roadside props are spread thinly.

Distance fog is present in all frames. In the coast frame it turns into a milky haze that washes out the whole image instead of only the far distance. The canyon frame's warm haze toward the vanishing point works best.

The asphalt has a noisy grain texture that reads as road. The sea is stylised blue streaks. The canyon walls are untextured colour bands. The building windows are a flat stripe texture, and the car's tail lamps and wheels read as plain white blobs.

The roadster has a believable silhouette with roll hoops and a stripe livery. The trees, rocks and houses are low-poly generated props whose style does not match the car. The tail-lamp housings and wheels lack detail.

The car sits in the lower-right third and takes about 12 to 15% of the frame. The horizon and finish gantry sit dead centre in every shot, and the large empty sky or wall areas carry no visual interest.
The chase camera is low with a field of view of roughly 60° and the same offset in every frame. The car sits to the right of the lane centre with no visible speed framing or lean.

The coast frame has lifted blacks and low contrast with no filmic tone curve. The canyon and night frames show only a mild vignette and grain. The tyre smoke puffs at the bottom right are flat grey discs.

nextChange.change: raise shadow strength toward the look target and pull the key light to an angle that throws visible contact shadows
